headline: The truck became the till
lede: FLOOR BOSS got its freight line: packing no longer pays — money follows the freight onto the trailer, full trailers earn a per-box bonus, and calling the truck early is a tax on impatience. Along the way the shifted timing surfaced two old law races, and both got fixed with proof.

notes.text: Escrow is the new dock: a packed order books its payout onto the parcel (blue HOLD chips, ESCROW readout in the HUD), and the cash-register rings only when the trailer hauls the last box. Stranded parcels pay nothing — reel the pad in before the whistle.
Full trailers (3+ boxes) earn 6 credits per box; manager tap-calls pay a 5-credit express fee while scheduled pickups stay free. Waiting for the pad became a real dock decision with a felt payoff.

The economy shift exposed two pre-existing bugs: a refused purchase froze the autopilot (held buttons never edge again — now it steps off and retries), and a robot repaired mid-swing raced the gantry (now it stands down). The reach-mutant also learned its pin from a literal, not the tunable constant.

Measured honestly: the autopilot wins 14/15 seeds averaging ~1197 throughput (was ~1160) — one thin seed lands short, and the README says so. Harness: 5/5 mutants die, 26/26 browser gates, books balance on every seed.
